fixes.explanation: Yes, baker, that's the second blank. The LORD says, “Obey Me, and I will be your God, and you will be My people.” (Jeremiah 7:23). The first half of that promise is about who He will be, and the second half is about who they will be. So people goes with “My.”
A guide is a nice word, friend, and I'd gladly follow one. But the LORD says, “…I will be your God…” (Jeremiah 7:23). That's what goes in the first blank.
I get why a judge came to mind with all this talk of anger. But the LORD says, “Obey Me, and I will be your God, and you will be My people.” (Jeremiah 7:23). The word He uses is God.

No army in this verse, baker. The LORD is speaking of what He commanded their fathers when He brought them out of Egypt: “Obey Me, and I will be your God, and you will be My people.” (Jeremiah 7:23). So the second blank is people, because they would belong to Him.

Nothing in this verse is about where Jeremiah, the prophet, lives. Earlier, the LORD tells him to stand at the gate and speak (Jeremiah 7:2). The thing he's told not to do here is pray: “…do not pray for these people…” (Jeremiah 7:16).

That's the one. The text says “…the women knead the dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven…” (Jeremiah 7:18). The sons gather wood and the fathers light the fire, so the whole family has a part. It's a heavy thing to read, friend.

Neighbors don't show up in this verse, baker. The LORD asks, “Is it not themselves they spite, to their own shame?” (Jeremiah 7:19). He's turning the question around, so the shame lands on the people doing it. That makes the blank themselves.

True, baker. The LORD says His anger and fury will be poured out on this place, “…and it will burn and not be extinguished.” (Jeremiah 7:20). The verse says the fire will not be put out. It's a serious line, so let's just let it sit.

That's a neat pattern, but the verse doesn't give one. The LORD says He sent His servants the prophets “…again and again.” (Jeremiah 7:25). The text doesn't say how many came or when, so I won't put a number on it.

A seven-year schedule makes sense as a guess, baker, but the text doesn't set one. The LORD says, “…I have sent you all My servants the prophets again and again.” (Jeremiah 7:25). That covers the time from the day their fathers came out of Egypt until that day. No schedule is given, just again and again.

Yes, baker. The message says, “Truth has perished; it has disappeared from their lips.” (Jeremiah 7:28). It's the same sad point in two phrases. That's said about the nation that would not listen to the voice of the LORD their God.

I wish that were the word, friend. The message says the opposite: “Truth has perished; it has disappeared from their lips.” (Jeremiah 7:28). Returned would mean truth came back, but the line says it has disappeared.

The verse doesn't mention a king at all, baker. The reason it gives is, “…for the LORD has rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath.” (Jeremiah 7:29). So the lament is about the LORD's rejection, not a battle.

Rebuilding sounds like a good thing, baker, but it's not what the verse says. The LORD says they set up their abominations in the house that bears His Name, “…and so have defiled it.” (Jeremiah 7:30). The word the verse uses is defiled.

It sounds right, but it isn't what the verse says, friend. The LORD says this place will no longer be called Topheth and the Valley of Ben-hinnom, “…but the Valley of Slaughter.” (Jeremiah 7:32). That's the new name He gives it.
That's a real valley name (Joshua 7:26), baker, but it isn't the one in this verse. The LORD says the place will be called “…the Valley of Slaughter.” (Jeremiah 7:32). That's the new name here.

The verse doesn't mention a king or a ban on weddings, baker. It says the voices of the bride and bridegroom will be removed, “…for the land will become a wasteland.” (Jeremiah 7:34). That's the reason the text gives.

Yes, baker. The host of heaven are what “…they have loved, served, followed, consulted, and worshiped.” (Jeremiah 8:2). The text gives a whole list, and loved and served are on it. The LORD says the bones will be exposed to the sun and moon and all the host of heaven.
